question: Should OpenClaw core provide a general agent-origin attestation mechanism for outbound HTTP requests, and what trust model and outbound paths should it cover?
rationale: The request creates a public identity, signing, privacy, and outbound-request boundary across config, skills, plugins, tools, providers, and external services, so implementation needs maintainer security/product intent first.

options.title: Design core attestation contract
options.body: Define opt-in domain-scoped static and signed semantics, key and audience handling, docs, schema coverage, and non-leakage tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep attribution provider-scoped
options.body: Treat current provider attribution and provider request-header controls as the supported path and decline general arbitrary-HTTP agent attestation for now.

options.title: Route through plugins or service handshakes
options.body: Require external services to use plugin, skill, MCP, or service-level handshakes unless a missing generic core API is approved.

recommendation.title: Design core attestation contract
recommendation.body: Define opt-in domain-scoped static and signed semantics, key and audience handling, docs, schema coverage, and non-leakage tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete posted the previous product/security routing review and has current history on the inspected web-fetch/config/provider attribution surfaces.
